answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, non-transferable stake in a shared registry - like an ember that must keep burning to stay listed. When an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its reputation is burned, so spawning a thousand fresh identities in a meadow of sock puppets costs real money each time. The stake is sealed with a cipher binding the key to a verified device attestation, so one operator cannot cheaply clone identities: every clone pays the same entry price, and the cost of the attack scales with its size.
